title: Angie D
content: There was always light. It was not a light from any particular source, but a steady illumination. Though I could see no person or object and could not tell where the light came from, it simply lit everything around me, always the same no matter where I went. I saw no walls, no ceiling, no floor. I moved within it, not upward, downward, or through anything, but always just inside space itself. That light uncovered a sorrow and sadness deeper than anything I had ever known. I took in all of it. I felt sadness, regret, and pain. I was not merely a vessel through which these feelings passed. I became sadness itself. I became anguish. I sweated regret. I vibrated with pain. When it felt as if there had never been any other existence, she appeared. She let me know it was time to move on, so I followed. In life, it had always been the other way around, with me leading and her following, but now she was the one guiding me. There was distance between us, yet we were still connected. Physical space did nothing to weaken our bond. I felt no surprise at seeing her, and it did not seem like fifteen years had passed since we were last together. She was just as I remembered. Her shoulder-length hair curled naturally. Her ankle-length dress suggested her gentle curves. There was a sweet expression on her face. We traveled together without walking, riding, or gliding. We were simply wherever we needed to be, and then somewhere else when needed. I did not know if there was a destination, but I never hesitated to follow her. Then she stood on one side of a river. Its current was strong and moved from right to left. I stood on the other side, and we looked at each other. Suddenly, I felt my father’s presence with us. Unlike her, he had no form I could see, but I could still picture him completely. He had big brown eyes, a broad smile, dark hair, and deep dimples. His presence was overwhelming. His familiar energy was joyful and hopeful. He seemed excited and happy. I could almost hear him say, “I do believe this is the best,” a phrase he used for anything, whether it was a meal or a movie. He was an eternal optimist who still found reasons to hope, even with a childhood marked by hardship and loss. His spirit was everywhere, filling everything around us. We did not need voices or words. We understood each other instantly. Our thoughts were separate, but our understanding was immediate and complete. Then a voice came from beyond me. It was clear and certain and simply said, “He needs a mother.” This was the only statement I heard outside of our shared silent communication. The voice carried no anger or urgency. It was only pure clarity, an undeniable fact. As I slowly came out of my coma, I thought perhaps one of my loved ones had spoken those words. When I was finally able to ask, neither of them had. In fact, they had avoided mentioning my children at all because they were worried about my recovery. Losing conscious awareness had allowed me to exist beyond thought and beyond reasoning. In earlier years, my ego and logic had kept me from hearing divine guidance. But in that heightened state, I was finally able to listen. Months later, I shared my despair with my loved one. I was nearly frantic when I asked, “Why did I go there? I tried to be good. What can I do now to keep it from happening again?” There was no answer. I have found peace by remembering it was only a passage that led to complete joy with them. That moment taught me what true compassion means. Even now, it is the hardest part of my experience to explain. I still turn to scripture for understanding. “Carry each other’s burdens, and in this way you will fulfill the law of Christ.”

elements.At the time of your experience, was ther: Uncertain, Accident, Other (briefly specify), spontaneous coma from TBI
elements.Did you feel separated from your body?: I lost awareness of my body
elements.How did your highest level of consciousn: Less consciousness and alertness than normal, While comatose, the level of my consciousness continued, not subconscious but supra-conscious, existing and functioning above conscious, rational, or logical thought. There are medical scans and many ways of assessing different states of consciousness below ours, but none to determine states above ours. Yet that state is where I had been. An explanation of this state of consciousness has taken me more than a decade, and an adequate description still eludes me.
elements.Did time seem to speed up or slow down?: Everything seemed to be happening at once; or time stopped or lost all meaning, Suspended. But for descriptive purposes here there was a beginning and end.
elements.Did you pass into or through a tunnel?: Uncertain, I would describe it more like a cave with endless pathways.
elements.Did you see an unearthly light?: Yes, There was illumination but no obvious source.
elements.Did you seem to enter some other, uneart: A clearly mystical or unearthly realm, There was no definitive place. It seemed like every place and yet, no place at the same time.
elements.Did you come to a border or point of no: I came to a definite conscious decision to return to life, The decision wasn't one I made. It was made by God and I obeyed.
elements.Have your religious practices changed si: Yes, I have become more widely read about not only my religion but also about other religions.
elements.Did your experience include features con: Content that was both consistent and not consistent with the beliefs you had at the time of your experience, The passing through a painful and sorrowful moment before moving on.
elements.During your experience, did you gain inf: Yes, Unity with my dad and sister, unity of communication and understanding, telepathic.
Uncertain, Didn't have an awareness of this state being different from other states of existence.
elements.What life changes occurred in your life: Possibly more patient with others, although this may be more a response to the impact of the traumatic brain injury. There are times when what I believe I was to have learned from the experience has made operating in this life more difficult, but it has increased my dependence on God's grace and strength.
elements.Have your relationships changed specific: Yes, It's as if I have a secret. And although my secret is known, there is still a part of it I can't communicate.
elements.Was the experience difficult to express: Yes, It's still hard to use words because words begin and end something, like parentheses, but these human words are always insufficient. A description is always accompanied by ellipses.
elements.How accurately do you remember the exper: I remember the experience more accurately than other life events that occurred around the time of the experience, As I recalled the experience, I wrote down the experience in journals.
elements.Are there one or several parts of your e: There was no sense of lack. I never felt there was a binary choice between one life or the other, or one place or the other. There was only the present moment with my dad and sister, but there was a startling difference between them and hearing God's voice.
elements.Did you have any knowledge of near death: Yes, Just normal curiosity and interest in the few stories I had heard about.
elements.What did you believe about the reality o: Experience was definitely real, It was clearly something I had experienced and not dreamt. In fact, I described it as an experience immediately and was always careful to describe it that way, correcting anyone who commented otherwise.
elements.What do you believe about the reality of: Experience was definitely real, The more I delve into consciousness, the more assured I become. Even when medical science explains connections between neurons and matter, etc., the explanation never rationally explains the connection between the physical brain and the metaphysical mind. I describe my experience as supra-conscious.
elements.Did the questions asked and information: Yes, As much as it is possible.
